meta.title: Training principles
meta.description: Fundamental aikido training principles established by the founder Morihei Ueshiba.

intro: Morihei Ueshiba, the founder of aikido, established fundamental principles for training that remain valid to this day.

principles.strong: Aikido decides between life and death with a single strike.
principles.text: During practice, follow the instructor's guidance and do not try to force techniques.

principles.strong: Aikido is the way by which one defeats a thousand enemies.
principles.text: Even when practicing with a single partner, be prepared for an attack from any direction.
Practice in a spirit of mutual respect and joy of movement.

principles.strong: The teacher can only teach you a small part.
principles.text: You must acquire most of the art through your own diligent practice and reflection.

principles.strong: Daily practice begins with a warm-up
principles.text: and gradually increase the intensity. Do not overexert yourself. Even older people can practice with joy and without injury.

principles.strong: The purpose of aikido is to train both body and mind
principles.text: and to develop sincere, honorable people. The techniques are sacred and must not be shown to the uninitiated.
